premises_considered.logline: The Inspector investigates a desk-drawer cable knot and unties it with a box; the box is the tidy ending but she is merely a bystander.
premises_considered.why_not: Violates the show rule: she is not exposed as culprit, and the product is a cleanup tool rather than the comic mechanism.

premises_considered.logline: The Inspector reviews 'before and after' of a cable mess and declares the box a success.
premises_considered.why_not: Reads as testimonial and implies a user result; forbidden claims and no firsthand endorsement.

premises_considered.logline: The Inspector sweeps six suspect cables into a box that holds up to six; the box's stated limit is the lie detector: a seventh cable will not fit, and it is the one running from her own chest lamp.
The Inspector tests how many cables the box can hold by cramming extras in until it bursts.
premises_considered.why_not: Invents a durability or stress claim, which is forbidden, and turns the product into the butt of the joke.

selected_premise.logline: The Inspector rounds up six suspect cables behind a side table into a six-cable box, then the lid will not close on a seventh: the charging lead of her own inspection lamp.
selected_premise.audience_emotion: Smug anticipation turning into delighted 'of course it's her'.
selected_premise.character_desire: To close the Cable Incident cleanly with every offending cable contained.
selected_premise.obstacle: The lid will not close; one cable too many remains, and she cannot find its source.
selected_premise.escalation: She tags each of six cables with safety-orange tape and counts them in; the lid still rises a centimetre, so she recounts and traces the extra lead with her lamp beam.
selected_premise.surprise: The camera drifts down her jacket and follows the lead to her own chest lamp and the wall socket; she is tethered to the scene.
selected_premise.payoff: The box holds the six and her own lead is the seventh offender; she names herself, unplugs her lamp and the lid closes.
selected_premise.why_send_it: A clean, silent-readable gag: product limit (holds up to six) is the only fact used and it directly causes the reveal. The rule is honoured and no one claims to have used the box.

script.title: Seventh Offender
script.synopsis: The Inspector tags six suspect cables and sorts them into a cable box that holds up to six. The lid will not close. A seventh lead runs down from her own chest lamp to the wall. She names the culprit: herself.

beats.beat: Lamp beam finds a knot of six cables; tape rips; she declares an incident and six suspects.
She tags each cable with orange tape and counts them into the open box.
Six cables are in, contained; she presses the lid but it lifts a centimetre.
She hunts the extra lead with her beam; the camera drifts down her jacket to her own lamp lead plugged into the wall.
She unplugs her lamp and the lid clicks shut; she taps her clipboard and names the offender.
A deadpan disclosure after the verdict.
